idea-plugin.name: MockkHttp
idea-plugin.description:
Network Traffic Interceptor for Android & Flutter Development

Capture, debug and mock HTTP/HTTPS traffic from Android and Flutter apps — including Flutter on iOS Simulators. Everything happens inside the app via lightweight interceptors: no proxy, no certificates, no root.

Supported Platforms:

  • Android (native): any OkHttp/Retrofit app — the interceptor is auto-injected by the Gradle plugin; emulators and physical devices
  • Flutter (Android): the mockk_http package intercepts dart:io HttpClient, package:http and dio
  • Flutter (iOS): iOS Simulators work with zero config; physical iPhones via MockkHttp.init(host: ...)

Key Features:

  • Recording Mode: view all HTTP requests and responses in real time, with search, request/response bodies and copy-as-cURL
  • Debug Mode: pause any request and edit the response (status, headers, body) before the app receives it
  • Mockk Mode: auto-apply mock rules — the app gets the mock without hitting the real server
  • Mock Collections: organize rules in collections, enable/disable with one click, export/import as JSON with smart merge
  • Zero-Config Interception: Gradle plugin injects the interceptor automatically — no code changes needed
  • Works with Certificate Pinning: interception happens inside the app, so there is no TLS man-in-the-middle to break pinning
  • Debug Builds Only: automatically excluded from release builds (multiple security layers)
  • Failsafe Design: if the plugin server is not running, requests pass through untouched

Setup:

  • Android: add the io.github.sergiydev09.mockkhttp Gradle plugin to your app — that's it, no dependencies to declare
  • Flutter: add mockk_http to pubspec.yaml and call MockkHttp.init()

See the Help tab in the tool window for detailed setup instructions.

Requirements:

  • IntelliJ IDEA / Android Studio 2024.3 or newer
  • Android: Android SDK platform-tools (ADB); emulator or physical device (API 21+)
  • iOS (Flutter): macOS with Xcode 15+ for Simulators; physical devices best-effort

Use Cases:

  • Debug network issues in your app
  • Test error handling by mocking server errors
  • Inspect API responses without backend access
  • Document API contracts for your team
  • Test offline scenarios and edge cases

Note: This tool is designed for development and testing purposes only. The interceptor only works in debug builds and has minimal performance impact. Native iOS (Swift/URLSession) apps are not supported yet — iOS coverage is via Flutter.
